skill.name: reword
skill.description: Build a saved writing voice from chosen samples and explicit preferences. Use it to draft, rewrite, and review prose for different destinations.
skill.summary: Draft and edit in your writing voice with private collections, destination guidance, and local preservation checks.
skill.author: starrybodies

content.user_title: Write and Edit in Your Own Voice
content.value_statement: Generic rewrites can lose your writing voice or change important details. Reword uses chosen samples, saved preferences, and local checks to guide personalized drafting and editing.
actual_capabilities: Build private voice collections from deliberately supplied samples, with separate authored and reference labels.
Assemble bounded editing and voice-learning requests for the host model without bundled network calls.
Apply destination guidance for email, chat, text messages, LinkedIn, cover letters, essays, and web copy.
Compare drafts for changes to numbers, dates, quotations, code, links, locked phrases, and selected claim relationships.
Save explicit preferences and author revisions, with consent required for automatic feedback capture.
Inspect collection coverage, export compact voice cards, pause learning, forget evidence, and restore retained profile versions.
limitations: Writing and semantic voice distillation require a host model; Python helpers do not generate prose or train model weights.
Preservation checks are heuristics, not proof of truth or complete semantic equivalence; many language-sensitive checks target English.
Prose commands accept plain text and Markdown; rich documents, binary formats, and source code require other editing tools.
Voice fidelity is not guaranteed, and character budgets do not guarantee exact token counts.

use_cases.title: Keep Professional Messages Personal
use_cases.description: Rewrite emails and team messages using saved preferences while checking dates, requests, and commitments against the original.

use_cases.title: Draft Applications Without Invented Claims
use_cases.description: Use a personal voice guide and supplied career facts to draft cover letters with suitable destination conventions.

use_cases.title: Maintain an Editorial Voice
use_cases.description: Build a compact guide from selected authored pieces, then refine essay or web-copy guidance using deliberate revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite One Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this email for clarity while keeping my tone. Preserve all dates, names, and commitments. Return finished copy: [draft].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: edit without creating a saved voice collection.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Private Voice Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Build my voice from these authored samples: [samples]. Save a named collection in my chosen private location. Ask before enabling ongoing learning.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a collection from deliberately selected writing.

prompt_templates.title: Draft for a Specific Destination
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my selected voice collection to draft a cover letter from [factual brief] for [reader]. Use only supplied facts. Apply my explicit preferences: [preferences].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: combine a saved voice with destination guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refine and Verify a Voice Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this author revision once: [original and revision]. Keep ongoing learning disabled. Refresh email guidance within the evidence budget. Show pending evidence and export the compact card.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: update scoped guidance while retaining consent and inspection controls.

output_examples.input: Rewrite this email directly: I am writing to ask whether you could review the draft by Friday.
output_examples.output: Could you review the draft by Friday?

output_examples.input: Draft an update in a direct voice using only these facts: the booking form is live; two reported issues remain under review.
output_examples.output: The booking form is live. We are still reviewing two reported issues.

output_examples.input: Compare the original deadline of November 18 with a candidate that changes it to November 20.
output_examples.output: Blocking difference: the deadline changed from November 18 to November 20. Restore the original date before replacing the source.

best_practices: Choose relevant authored samples, label reference inspiration separately, and keep collections outside public repositories.
State the destination, reader, factual brief, and explicit preferences before drafting or editing.
Preserve originals and review the comparison using the same voice and destination settings before replacement.
anti_patterns: Treating sample experiences or reference writing as factual support for a new draft.
Enabling ongoing learning without consent or treating accepted model prose as authored evidence.
Assuming a clear mechanical check proves factual accuracy, complete meaning preservation, or an exact voice match.

faq.question: Does Reword send my writing to a separate service?
faq.answer: The bundled Python helpers make no network calls. Writing and voice distillation use your host model, whose processing and privacy rules still apply.

faq.question: What does the host need?
faq.answer: The host must read skill files and use a writing model. Full local functionality also needs Python 3.10 or later and durable private storage.

faq.question: How many samples should I provide?
faq.answer: You can start with one deliberately chosen piece. Three to five relevant authored pieces provide more material, but do not guarantee voice fidelity.

faq.question: Does creating a collection enable ongoing learning?
faq.answer: No. Ongoing learning requires a separate opt-in. You can save a requested correction once without enabling automatic future updates.

faq.question: Can I inspect or remove saved material?
faq.answer: You can inspect coverage, export a compact guide, pause learning, forget evidence, and restore retained profile versions. Forgetting also clears derived profiles and history.

faq.question: Do the checks guarantee that an edit is accurate?
faq.answer: No. They flag selected protected-content changes and claim risks. Review meaning, facts, and style against the original before accepting an edit.
